name: Unibot router unvalidated external call
summary: The direct Unibot router's externally callable function 0xb2bd16ab accepted an unvalidated external target and calldata without binding the token owner to the caller or an authorized Unibot operator. It therefore made attacker-selected transferFrom calls as the approved router, allowing the original exploiter to pull tokens from wallets that had approved it.

loss.notes: This record covers only the original 0x413e4f... exploiter's Ethereum campaign; later copycats are not added. Its 22 successful drain transactions run from the anchor through 0x3efea1... at block 18468232:28. Receipt and call-trace enumeration finds 299 successful victim-to-attacker transferFrom calls and matching Transfer logs, spanning 254 unique victim addresses and 22 token contracts. The often-reported 364-victim/42-token counts therefore appear to include attempted entries or broader activity and are not used as exact loss components. The attacker sold the stolen tokens through block 18468489 and then made 18 Tornado Cash deposits totaling exactly 355.5 ETH: three 100 ETH, five 10 ETH, five 1 ETH, and five 0.1 ETH deposits. CertiK independently reports 355.5 ETH of realized proceeds. This conservative realized-extraction measure avoids inventing incident prices for 22 mostly illiquid source tokens; swaps, copycat proceeds, and the team's later victim reimbursements are not added or netted against gross loss. DefiLlama's ETH observation 28 seconds before the anchor is 1800.0036569996832 USD, giving 639901.3000633874 USD and explaining the seed row's rounded 640000 USD figure.

ageReset.description: Transaction 0xca799f...5724b directly created router 0x126c9f...1865. Its code is absent at block 18450357 and its 23,718-byte runtime has hash 0x16524e...5521c at both block 18450358 and the pre-anchor block 18467789. The anchor trace calls that address directly 17 times and shows no DELEGATECALL from it, while the EIP-1967 implementation and beacon slots are zero.

sources.note: Reviewed the original exploiter's complete Ethereum account history, all 22 successful drain-transaction receipts and call traces, the immediately preceding helper deployment trace, router creation transaction and receipt, historical runtime bytecode, EIP-1967 slots, pinned reproduction, technical reports, official project response, all subsequent sale transactions, and the 18 Tornado deposits. Helper deployment 0x86f0f4...fedf makes no router call. Transaction 0x9c0503...8a00 is the next transaction and the earliest successful one that executes the defect: its helper calls router 0x126c9fbab3a2fca24edfd17322e71a5e36e91865 17 times through selector 0xb2bd16ab, and the router makes 17 successful transferFrom calls. Across the full campaign, traces and receipts contain 299 successful pulls from 254 unique victim addresses across 22 token contracts; the last is 0x3efea1...9fc0 at block 18468232:28. The direct router was created at block 18450358:92 by 0x40800a492a04ae99c7fa6a0c2b52e3beb6675a0d, has no code in the preceding block, has unchanged runtime hash 0x16524eee2f99bba009889f1a947067c967bc360f1c321d16b2a070d71525521c through the pre-anchor block, and performs no DELEGATECALL in the exploit trace. After selling the stolen tokens, the exploiter deposited exactly 355.5 ETH into Tornado Cash in 18 transactions; this matches CertiK's independent proceeds figure.
